historical_evidence.finding: observed within-game change 61.0% and cross-game change 67.7%; 99.0% of units and 100% of series show a change; transition matrices near-uniform; but inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offensive execution, labeling error noted.
first-half play-type usage predicts second-half suppression only weakly; predictive lift over mean reversion is +0.039; bulk of H2 suppression is regression to the mean.
RTM explains 32.9% of variance in H1->H2 PPP collapse; additional usage, process, lineup, context explain only ~1.7pp; remaining 65.4% is unexplained bewezen noise.
teams that abandon a suppressed play type show smaller matched-pair excess decline than those that continue; but reconstructed post-hoc cohort and small sample (n=255) limits inference.

failed_approaches.what_failed: using inferred labels for defensive adjustment
failed_approaches.why: label error – inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offensive execution

failed_approaches.what_failed: testing H1 usage as predictor of H2 suppression
failed_approaches.why: RTM selection – predictive lift over mean reversion is minimal, indicating regression to the mean dominates

failed_approaches.what_failed: explaining variance of H1->H2 PPP collapse beyond RTM
failed_approaches.why: B_powered_null – additional factors explain negligible variance, leaving majority unexplained

failed_approaches.what_failed: matched-pair comparison of adapt vs continue teams
failed_approaches.why: unanswerable – post-hoc cohort design and small sample preclude valid inference

evidence_establishes: Defensive adjustments occur frequently within and across games, but labeling issues hamper precise measurement; H2 suppression largely reflects regression to the mean rather than strategic adjustment; additional contextual factors explain only a small fraction of suppression variance.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a defense’s effect on opponents’ H2-H1 change is a stable, reliable team trait across seasons; whether defensive adjustment can be measured with sufficient precision to detect a consistent team effect.
own_inferences: The data set provides ample per-game possessions but suffers from labeling noise and regression-to-the-mean confounding, making it unlikely to reliably capture a defensive trait. A multi-season, matched-pair design controlling for opponent strength and league averages would be required, but power remains marginal.
uncertainties: No evidence of team-season reliability for defensive effects; potential hidden confounders such as coaching changes or roster shifts; measurement reliability of H2-H1 change not directly validated.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical studies show defensive adjustments are inconsistent, heavily confounded by regression to the mean, and suffer labeling errors. This evidence suggests the research question cannot be answered with the available data at useful power, leading to a decision not to proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: Labeling of defensive adjustment is unreliable; inferred labels cannot isolate true defensive strategies.
Regression to the mean dominates H2 suppression, masking true defensive effects.
H2-H1 change measurement is noisy and may vary within games.
Opponent strength, coaching changes, and roster composition may confound observed defensive effects.

prior_work.summary: Prior studies indicate defensive adjustments occur but are largely confounded by regression to the mean and label noise, leaving the reliability of a defensive trait unproven.

risks.text: Inferred defensive labels cannot distinguish real adjustments from offensive execution.
Regression to the mean explains most of the observed H2 suppression.
H2-H1 change may be subject to measurement noise within games.
Opponent strength and roster changes may bias defensive effect estimates.

design.estimand: Effect of a team’s defensive adjustment on opponents’ H2-H1 change, measured as the difference in H2-H1 change between games where the defense shows a defensive adjustment vs games without adjustment, controlling for opponent average and league context
design.power: Low – estimated power <0.3 for detecting small to medium effects given current labeling reliability
design.controls: Opponent average H2-H1 change, league average, season year, and defensive adjustment indicator
design.falsification: Compare to random assignment of defensive adjustment indicator; test if estimated effect disappears when shuffled
design.decision_rule: Reject null if 95% CI excludes 0; otherwise fail to reject
